scenario.name: Afternoon claim on the shared conference room
scenario.audience: A staff member who needs the department conference room
scenario.objective: Check the room's calendar for a free window, claim it, and see a clashing claim refused while a cancellation reopens the time.
workflow: Open the room's week view and read its existing reservation blocks as busy time
Submit a 14:00-16:00 claim for Thursday with a purpose note
Submit a second overlapping claim and receive a refusal naming the conflict
Cancel the original claim and confirm the slot shows free again
acceptance: The week view shows each accepted claim against the named room
An overlapping claim for the same room is refused and no block is added
Cancelling removes the block so the 14:00-16:00 window reads free

issues: acceptance/probe.py:156-172 (A02) never verifies that the rejected zero-length claim added no row. After the 400 response it calls only touching() (lines 91-92), whose strict overlap test cannot see a 14:00-14:00 ghost against 14:00-16:00, and the later exactly-once check counts only the new id. A server that returns 400 but also inserts the zero-length row still passes, contrary to AUTHOR_INPUT.json:13 ('adds nothing') and the A02 goal 'creates no block'.

acceptance/probe.py:157 requires the zero-length rejection to be exactly INVALID_INTERVAL, but VIEW_ARCH.md:86 lists both INVALID_INTERVAL and INVALID_DURATION and VIEW_ARCH.md:92 only states a duration of 30-240 minutes. A spec-following implementation can reasonably return 400 INVALID_DURATION, while AUTHOR_INPUT.json:13 requires only 400; the probe is stricter than the pinned contract.

acceptance/probe.py:185-188 checks only that error.conflicts contains the original id and that error.message contains that id. It never verifies conflicting start/end values. VIEW_ARCH.md:88 requires error.conflicts objects with id/start/end and a message naming both intervals, and AUTHOR_INPUT.json:14 requires naming the 14:00-16:00 reservation and its times; an implementation returning only the id passes A03.

acceptance/README.md:21,40 and VIEW_ARCH.md:114 claim the probe checks both fixed windows before writing and exits 2 with status not_run when setup is unsafe. The probe instead checks 09:00-10:00 inside A01 and creates it (probe.py:134-135), then checks 14:00-16:00 only later in A02 (probe.py:158-160). If 14:00 is occupied, the 09:00 probe claim may already have been written, and occupied windows become failed cases with exit 1, not not_run; exit 2 is used only for the initial GET failure (probe.py:101-107).
review.summary: The leaf scope, source citations, and design distinction are sound, and the Thursday claim/conflict/cancel journey is covered end to end. The acceptance layer has blocking contract gaps: A02 does not verify that the zero-length refusal leaves no row, A02 hardcodes an error code the architecture does not pin, A03 does not verify the conflict times required by the API, and the documented not_run/refuse-to-proceed safety behavior is not implemented because the probe can write the 09:00 claim before discovering that 14:00 is occupied.
